verdict.summary: Connecting your own Gmail account through your own Google OAuth client takes minutes to hours. Public use is hard because the Gmail scopes that read, compose or modify mail are restricted, which requires Google restricted-scope verification and, if your server stores or transmits Gmail data, an annual CASA security assessment. Send-only or labels-only features need far less review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Gate 1 and 2 setup: about 1-3 hours. Gate 3 (privacy policy, scope justifications, domain and brand verification, demo video, CASA, submission): several days to weeks of active work.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 1 hour for your own account (estimate, not sourced).
verdict.approval_wait: Google estimates about 6 weeks for restricted-scope verification, with the caveat that estimates vary with developer responsiveness. CASA timing was not found. No measured timelines were found.

gates.name: Testing status, your own account only
gates.unlocks: Your own Google account can authorize the app while the consent screen is in Testing. No verification needed for development or testing apps.
limits: Apps in development or testing do not need verification unless launched publicly.
Restricted scopes still trigger the tester warning screen, a user cap, and a limited refresh-token lifetime while in Testing.

gates.name: Testing with test users (or Internal, for Workspace orgs)
gates.unlocks: Up to 100 named test users can authorize the app. Internal user type is available only inside a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization.
limits: Up to 100 test users listed on the consent screen.
Test-user authorizations expire 7 days after consent, unless the app requests only openid/userinfo.email/userinfo.profile.
Unverified-app screen shows when sensitive or restricted scopes are used without completed verification.
New-user cap of 100 applies over the project's entire lifetime and cannot be reset.
Internal user type cannot serve plain @gmail.com accounts; Workspace admins may restrict access.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1, once test users are added.

gates.name: Production, verified (public)
gates.unlocks: Anyone can authorize the app with no unverified screen and no user cap, once Google approves restricted-scope verification.
limits: Requires Publish App to Production before Prepare for Verification.
Restricted scopes require verification; apps that store or transmit restricted data on servers also need an annual CASA security assessment.
Brand verification results are valid for 7 days; publish branding within that window or re-run it.
Changing redirect URLs or product name after verification requires re-verification.
gates.time_to_reach: Estimated about 6 weeks for restricted-scope verification per Google's FAQ, plus CASA assessment if required. Not guaranteed.

steps.title: Choose managed Composio auth or your own Google OAuth client
steps.detail: Composio offers managed OAuth for Gmail, so you can start without registering a Google client. Choose your own client only if you need your own consent screen, branding or verification path. If you use your own client, keep the scope set narrow, because Composio's default set includes the restricted full-access mail scope.
gotchas: Composio's default scope set includes https://mail.google.com/, which Google classifies as restricted and which Google says to request only for immediate permanent deletion.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API and set up the consent screen
steps.detail: Sign in with a Google account and open the Cloud Console consent page at https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials/consent. Select or create a project, enable the Gmail API from the API Library, then fill in the OAuth consent screen fields: user type, app name, support email, logo, home page, privacy policy, Terms of Service, authorized domains and developer contact information.
gotchas: The consent page sits behind a Google sign-in wall, so it only opens with a signed-in Google account.
Billing may be requested when enabling APIs.

steps.title: Declare only the scopes the feature needs
steps.detail: Add scopes on the Data Access page of the consent screen. Start from the narrowest scope that supports the feature, and declare every scope your code sends. Google groups scopes as sensitive or restricted, so check the tier of each one before you add it.
gotchas: Google checks every restricted scope declared on the consent screen, even if the code does not use it. Remove unused scopes before review.
Scopes in your code must match the consent screen, or users see the unverified-app screen.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client and set the Redirect URI
steps.detail: If you use your own client, create an OAuth client ID in Cloud Console and set the Authorized redirect URI to the value below. Google's discovery document confirms the authorize and token endpoints, so Composio's Google endpoints are the standard ones. Copy the client ID and client secret into your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Changing redirect URLs after verification forces you through verification again, so set the final callback before you submit.

steps.title: Connect your own Gmail account (Gate 1 test)
steps.detail: Start an authorization from your Composio auth config or your app using your own Gmail account. Confirm the consent screen lists only the scopes you intend to request. This is the first connection that proves Gate 1 works.
gotchas: Scopes requested in code must match the consent screen, or Google shows the unverified-app screen.

steps.title: Add test users and check token expiry (Gate 2)
steps.detail: While the consent screen is in Testing, add each tester on the test-user list (up to 100). Expect test-user authorizations to expire after 7 days, and plan to re-authorize. Test users are the only people who can authorize the app in this gate.
gotchas: Each test user consumes quota once added.
The 100-user cap is a lifetime cap for the project, so testers you use up cannot be reclaimed.

steps.title: Choose Internal or External user type
steps.detail: Choose Internal only if all users are in one Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization. Internal avoids verification and the user cap but cannot serve plain @gmail.com accounts. Workspace administrators may also restrict access to clients they have not marked as trusted.
gotchas: Internal user type can require admin configuration for restricted Gmail scopes.

steps.title: Draft verification materials
steps.detail: An agent can draft the privacy policy text, a scope justification for each restricted or sensitive scope (including why narrower scopes would not work), the limited-use statement, and a demo script that shows the consent screen with the exact scopes and each feature using them. The developer must review and publish the privacy policy on the same domain as the home page.
gotchas: Google data from restricted scopes may only be used for user-facing features; it may not be used to train or improve foundational AI models.
Insufficient justification can lead to rejection, and rejected requests need all materials resubmitted.

steps.title: Verify domain and brand, then publish to Production
steps.detail: Verify your domain in Google Search Console using an account that is a Project Owner or Editor. On the OAuth Branding page, complete app branding, run Verify Branding, then publish. Then click Publish App to move from Testing to Production, which is required before verification. Your homepage must be on the verified domain, describe the app, and not be only a login page.
gotchas: Brand verification results expire after 7 days if branding is not published; re-run it if you miss that window.
Google will not approve until domain ownership is verified.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record an English video of the OAuth grant flow. The video must show the App Name and OAuth client ID in the address bar, the full consent screen with the exact scopes, and each feature that uses a sensitive or restricted scope. Upload it to YouTube Studio and set Visibility to Unlisted.
gotchas: The video must show the same app and branding you submitted.

steps.title: Decide on a CASA security assessment
steps.detail: If your server stores or transmits Gmail data, you need a CASA security assessment by an independent CASA-authorized assessor. Google does not charge a fee for it, but you agree the assessor's cost directly with them. The assessment is annual. Assurance level depends on the data sensitivity, users per data type and other risk signals.
gotchas: Cost and tier thresholds were not found in the sources; get a quote from an assessor before you commit.

steps.title: Clean up OAuth clients and submit for verification
steps.detail: Remove or prepare every non-production OAuth client in the project, because all clients in a project requesting restricted scopes must be ready for review. Keep the project contact details current, because all review communications go by email to owners and editors. Then open the consent screen and click Submit for Verification.
gotchas: If a request is rejected, resubmit from the consent screen with Submit for Verification and resend all materials.

steps.title: Wait for review
steps.detail: Google reviews the scopes, justifications and video. Google's FAQ estimates 6 weeks for restricted-scope verification, and the sensitive-scope page gives 3-5 business days for sensitive scopes. Respond quickly to reviewer emails, because delays are tied to developer responsiveness.
steps.est_time: Estimated about 6 weeks for restricted scopes (not guaranteed)
gotchas: The FAQ says 10 business days for sensitive scopes, which conflicts with the 3-5 business days on the sensitive-scope page.

steps.title: Roll out and handle existing users
steps.detail: After approval, the app can be used publicly. Scopes added after a user has consented do not apply to that user until they re-consent, so plan a re-consent prompt if you add scopes later. Any change to redirect URLs or product name requires a new verification.
gotchas: Adding a Gmail scope to an existing grant does not grant it to connected users.

scopes.effect: Full mailbox access. Google says request only if the app must permanently delete messages bypassing Trash. Composio's default set includes it. Any app requesting it needs restricted-scope verification.
Restricted. Triggers restricted-scope verification and, for server-stored data, a CASA assessment.

scopes.scope: gmail.compose, gmail.modify, gmail.insert, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing
scopes.effect: Restricted. Same verification and CASA implications as gmail.readonly.
Sensitive, not restricted. Needs sensitive-scope verification and a justification and video, which Google estimates at 3-5 business days (FAQ says 10).
Non-sensitive per Google. No verification needed for this scope alone.
Using only these keeps the 7-day test-user expiry exception. Any other scope removes it.

scopes.scope: Composio default contacts, profile, address, birthday, phone and emails read scopes
scopes.effect: Not classified in the findings. Check each on Google's scopes page before you declare it on the consent screen.

blockers.symptom: Users see the unverified-app screen, and the app is capped at 100 users.
blockers.cause: The app requests sensitive or restricted scopes without completed verification, or code scopes do not match the consent screen.
blockers.fix: Trim scopes to the minimum needed, make code and consent screen scopes identical, or complete verification before public launch.

blockers.symptom: Verification is delayed or rejected even though the code does not use some restricted scopes.
blockers.cause: Google checks every restricted scope declared on the consent screen, including unused ones.
blockers.fix: Remove unused restricted scopes from the Data Access page before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Connected users still lack new Gmail access after you add a scope.
blockers.cause: Google only grants new scopes at consent time; existing grants are not updated.
blockers.fix: Prompt existing users to re-consent after you add scopes.

blockers.symptom: Verification request is rejected or needs to start over after a redirect URL change.
blockers.cause: Adding redirect URLs or JavaScript origins, or changing the product name, after verification requires a new verification.
blockers.fix: Finalize the Composio or custom callback URL before you submit.

blockers.symptom: Restricted-scope verification needs a CASA assessment you did not plan for.
blockers.cause: Your server stores or transmits restricted Gmail data, which triggers an annual CASA assessment.
blockers.fix: Decide early whether you store Gmail data server-side. If you do, budget for an assessor and an annual renewal.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth for Gmail if you only need Gate 1 or 2 testing; you do not need a Google Cloud client. Register your own Google OAuth client when you need your own branding, your own verification, or public use. Composio's default scopes include the restricted https://mail.google.com/ scope, so trim them to what the feature needs before you bring your own client to review. If you use your own client with Composio, the redirect URI is the Composio callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

open_questions: Review timelines conflict: the FAQ estimates 10 business days for sensitive-scope verification, while the sensitive-scope page says 3-5 business days. Restricted verification is estimated at 6 weeks. No measured timelines were found.
Google's redirect URI rules for web OAuth clients (schemes, localhost, wildcards) were not confirmed. Only the re-verification rule for changed redirect URLs was found.
Whether Google requires PKCE for a confidential Gmail web client was not confirmed. The discovery document only shows PKCE methods as supported.
The 6-month unused-refresh-token rule for In Production apps comes from a Google health-API page, not a Gmail-specific page. No Gmail-specific refresh-token page was fetched.
No Google source states a free vs paid developer account requirement, a partner program, or a business verification requirement for a Gmail OAuth app.
No install caps or rate limits specific to new unreviewed Gmail OAuth apps were found beyond the 100-user cap.
Google's Gmail API policy page, which defines permitted application types for restricted Gmail scopes, was not fetched.
Composio's managed OAuth for Gmail: whether Composio uses its own verified Google app, any user caps on Composio's side, and its exact redirect flow were not verified beyond toolkit metadata.
CASA tier thresholds (user counts per tier) and the assessor's cost were not found. Google says it does not charge the developer.
No Google documentation was found on product-level privacy-policy wording for Gmail data beyond the Limited Use rules and the FAQ example sentence.
Scope tiers for the Composio default contacts, profile, address, birthday, phone and emails scopes were not classified in the findings.
